To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we performed comprehensive genetic analyses in Japanese familial ALS patients using targeted next-generation sequencing, identified known and novel variants in ALS/motor neuron disease-related genes, and revealed considerable differences in the frequencies of genetic variations across populations.

we performed targeted next-genereation sequencing of ALS/motor neuron disease-related genes in Japanese familial ALS patients, and identified known and novel genetic variations in ALS2, ANG, OPT, SETX, SOD1, and TARDB, but not C9ORF2.
we identified novel variants of uncertain or likely pathogenicity in ALS2, ANG, OPT, SETX, TARDP, and VCP in a cohort of 51 Japanese patients with familial ALS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic causes of ALS.
the development of a new generation of targeted next-generation sequencing technology that can be used in clinical practice.
the genetic basis for familial ALS in Japan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
45% of the Japanese familial ALS cases have a known genetic mutation.
the frequency of the known pathogenic mutations was 48% (53/111) in Japanese familial ALS, and 52% (53/102) in familial ALS with a positive family history.
the genetic causes of familial ALS are diverse in Japan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic causes of familial ALS in Japan are diverse, but SOD1 and C9orf72 mutations are most common.
the frequency of known ALS-related variants in our Japanese cohort was 49% and that 1% of the familial ALS patients harbored a novel likely pathogenic variant in ALS2.
the frequency of known pathogenic variants in familial ALS in Japan is 46%, whereas the frequencies of variants of uncertain significance is 35%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of genetic variants in ALS is highly variable among populations.
the frequency and types of genetic variants in Japanese familial ALS patients are considerably different from other populations.
genetic analyses of familial ALS should be performed in a population-based manner.
